Some components read `props.name`, and others destructure `{ name }` first. With destructuring, the top of a component lists everything it uses. Without it, you always see where a value comes from. This rule makes your codebase stick to one style.

By default it asks for destructuring, in function components (`props`, `context`) and in class components (`this.props`, `this.state`, `this.context`).

`--fix` only works for `destructureInSignature`. It moves the destructuring into the parameter list.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/destructuring-assignment" = "error" # or "warn"
```

Every option, set to its default:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/destructuring-assignment" = [
  "error",
  "always", # "always" or "never"
  {
    ignoreClassFields = false,
    destructureInSignature = "ignore", # "always" or "ignore"
  },
]
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
function Badge(props) {
  return <span className={props.color}>{props.label}</span>;
}
```

{/* bad */}
```jsx
class Counter extends React.Component {
  render() {
    return <output>{this.state.count}</output>;
  }
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
function Badge({ color, label }) {
  return <span className={color}>{label}</span>;
}

class Counter extends React.Component {
  render() {
    const { count } = this.state;
    return <output>{count}</output>;
  }
}
```

Passing the whole object on is fine:

{/* good */}
```jsx
function Badge(props) {
  return <span {...props} />;
}
```

## Options

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/destructuring-assignment" = ["error", "always", {
  destructureInSignature = "always",
}]
```

The first option is `"always"` (default) or `"never"`. With `"never"`, the rule reports destructuring instead:

{/* bad {"options": ["never"]} */}
```jsx
function Badge({ color, label }) {
  return <span className={color}>{label}</span>;
}
```

The second option is an object. Both keys only matter with `"always"`:

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ignoreClassFields` | `false` | Allow `this.props.x` in a class field. |
| `destructureInSignature` | `"ignore"` | `"always"` reports `const { x } = props` in the body of a function component, unless `props` is also used somewhere else. |

{/* good {"options": ["always", {"ignoreClassFields": true}]} */}
```jsx
class Counter extends React.Component {
  state = { count: this.props.start };
  render() {
    const { count } = this.state;
    return <output>{count}</output>;
  }
}
```

{/* bad {"options": ["always", {"destructureInSignature": "always"}]} */}
```jsx
function Badge(props) {
  const { color, label } = props;
  return <span className={color}>{label}</span>;
}
```
